RESULT — bix-22-q2

HEADLINE ANSWER
Pearson correlation between gene length and mean CD4 expression, protein-coding genes:
  r = 0.0617  (full precision r = 0.0616970230,  r² = 0.003807,  p = 2.7728e-18,  n = 19,942 genes)
Weak positive correlation, statistically significant at n = 19,942 but essentially no explanatory power (~0.4% of variance).

Definition actually used (your rulings, hard-coded as R1–R6 comments in the script):
• CD4 = Sample_annotated_Zenodo.csv celltype == 'CD4' → 151 columns, matrix-column order preserved. Name-token match used only as an assert (passed, same 151).
• All 151 samples kept: both copies of L619 / L631 / A082, L367CD4 kept, no depth or dropout filtering.
• mean expression = arithmetic mean across those 151 columns of BatchCorrectedReadCounts, raw scale — no CPM/library-size normalisation, no log, no rank.
• Gene set = gene_biotype exactly 'protein_coding' → 19,942 genes; zero-mean genes kept; composite ';'-joined biotype strings excluded.
• Correlation = scipy.stats.pearsonr on (Length, mean_CD4), pairwise-complete rows.
• Length = field as tabulated in GeneMetaInfo (genomic-span vs exonic/transcript not determinable from the file — treated as an assumption, not a fact).

FINITE / NaN ACCOUNTING (you asked explicitly)
• Genes entering the correlation: 19,942; rows dropped as non-finite / pairwise-incomplete: 0; genes with NaN mean or NaN Length: 0.
• Every gene had all 151 samples contributing (min/max samples per gene = 151/151 — the matrix has no missing cells).
• pearsonr returned a FINITE r and p (asserted in the script): r = 0.06169702304001066, p = 2.7727567e-18. Median gene mean is 56.8 (protein-coding subset) and 1,518 zero-mean genes are retained — sparsity did not degenerate the statistic.

THREE-PATH AGREEMENT (guards against a parsing/rounding artefact)
• scipy.stats.pearsonr (headline):        0.061697023040
• manual covariance formula on a stdlib-csv re-parse of the matrix (no pandas read): 0.061697023040
• numpy.corrcoef on the written per-gene artifact: 0.061697023040
  max disagreement = 2.08e-17 → same number, all finite.

SENSITIVITY TABLE — explicitly NOT the answer (stability check of magnitude and sign)
variant                          n         value        p            note
drop zero-mean genes             18,424    0.0528200652 7.28e-13     sign/magnitude stable (−0.009 vs headline)
composite biotypes included      19,954    0.0616871725 2.74e-18     12 extra rows, negligible shift
148 de-duplicated CD4 samples    148 smp   0.0617134751 2.72e-18    donor collapse changes r in the 5th decimal
drop L367CD4 (lowest depth)      150 smp   0.0617002318 2.76e-18    no effect
log10(Length) vs log1p(mean)     19,942    0.4173023687 <1e-300     transformed scale — much larger (NOT reported as answer)
Spearman (rank transform)        19,942    0.4394251927 <1e-300     rank-based (NOT Pearson, NOT the answer)
Interpretation: the raw-scale Pearson is robust (0.053–0.062) to every sample/gene-set choice you ruled on; the only thing that moves it a lot is transform/rank, i.e. the length–expression relationship is monotone but strongly non-linear on the raw count scale. That is reported as context, not as an alternative answer.

STEPS ACTUALLY EXECUTED
1. Loaded all three tables; asserted shapes (59,453 × 723), unique IDs, index/column alignment.
2. Selected 151 CD4 columns via annotation celltype, asserted equality with the name-token set.
3. Computed the row-wise arithmetic mean over those 151 columns (float64, raw scale) — 0 NaN.
4. Inner-joined GeneMetaInfo on gene id (1:1, no aggregation), filtered exact 'protein_coding' → 19,942.
5. Pairwise-complete filter → 0 rows dropped, n = 19,942.
6. scipy.stats.pearsonr(Length, mean_CD4) → r = 0.0616970230, p = 2.7728e-18; finiteness asserted.
7. Wrote per-gene artifact (19,942 rows: Geneid, Chr, Length, gene_biotype, mean_CD4) and results JSON.
8. Ran the 6 sensitivity variants; wrote sensitivity CSV (labelled NOT-the-answer).
9. Re-derived r independently (stdlib CSV parse + covariance definition) and via numpy.corrcoef on the artifact; agreement 2e-17.

LIMITATIONS (one line each)
• "Length" is taken as tabulated; whether it is genomic span or exonic/transcript length is not recoverable from the file.
• No normalisation was applied per the ruling, so r is sensitive to library-size differences between CD4 samples (the 150-sample/dedup checks show this does not materially matter here).
• No covariate adjustment, batch correction, PCA or regression was performed — out of scope per your instruction; p-value is therefore unadjusted for multiple testing and treats genes as independent.

Artifacts (all regenerated by the executed run): analysis script, independent verification script, per-gene table, results JSON, sensitivity CSV, run log.
